description: One card on a dashboard, declared rather than programmed. The row says which list the number is counted from, what it is grouped by, which date column the dashboard's date range applies to and which rows are in scope before the range is applied — and one executor turns that into an ordinary list query. Because it is the SAME query the list itself runs, the number on the card and the number of rows behind it are the same answer, and every card is already narrowed to what the person looking at it is allowed to see. Nothing here grants or widens access. A chart is placed on a dashboard by a Dashboard Layout row, which points at this one by name, so editing a chart once changes it for every role that shows it.

fields.description: The short name a Dashboard Layout points at, in lower case letters, digits and underscores — for example leads_by_source. It cannot be changed once saved, because every layout showing this card names it by this word and would be left pointing at nothing.
fields.label: Chart Name

fields.description: The card's heading, in the words the person reading the dashboard uses. It is read from this row on every load, so renaming it moves the heading on every dashboard at once.
fields.label: Label

fields.description: A line under the heading saying what the number counts. Optional; left blank the card shows the heading alone.
fields.label: Subtitle

fields.description: A card that is not ticked is skipped everywhere — it is on no dashboard and is never queried, even where a layout still names it. This is how a card is taken down without editing every layout that shows it.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: The kind of card and the list it reads. Three kinds and two lists, deliberately: everything a card can be is something the executor already knows how to run, so a saved chart can never fail in a way only the dashboard finds out about.
fields.label: What It Is

fields.description: number is a single figure with no breakdown. donut and bar both break one figure down by a column and need Group By Field set; number must leave it empty.
fields.label: Chart Type

fields.description: The list the card counts. Leads and Activities are the two the executor runs, and it is a fixed choice rather than a free one so a card can never be pointed at a list nobody checked it against.
fields.label: Source List

fields.description: The figure itself, and — for a donut or a bar — the column it is broken down by.
fields.label: What Is Measured

fields.description: COUNT counts records and needs no column. SUM and AVG add up or average a numeric column, which then has to be named in Aggregate Field.
fields.label: Aggregate

fields.description: The column SUM or AVG is taken over. Required for those two and ignored for COUNT, which always counts records.
fields.label: Aggregate Field

fields.description: The column a donut or a bar is broken down by, written as a plain column name of the source list with no dots in it. It is also the column the drill-down filters on, which is why it has to be a real column of that list and not a column reached through another record.
fields.label: Group By Field

fields.description: An optional column to SHOW instead of the grouped value, and it may reach through a link — lead_owner.full_name shows a person's name where the group is their login. It changes the words on the slice and nothing else; the drill-down always filters on the grouped value itself.
fields.label: Label Field

fields.description: How many slices or bars the card shows, largest first. Ignored by a number card.
fields.label: Row Limit

fields.description: The rows in scope before anyone touches a filter, and whether the dashboard's date range applies to this card at all.
fields.label: Which Records Count

fields.description: The date column the dashboard's date range is applied to — creation, modified, due_date and so on. Different cards honestly date from different columns, so each one says which is its own.
fields.label: Date Field

fields.description: Ticked, the card answers for the chosen date range. Unticked it is a snapshot of right now and ignores the range entirely — which is what a card like Overdue Activities means, and saying so here is what stops a dashboard quietly mixing the two.
fields.label: Honours Date Range

fields.description: The rows this card is about, as an ordinary filter object — {"status": ["in", ["Backlog", "Todo"]]}. Three words stand for the moment the dashboard is opened rather than the moment this row was saved: __TODAY__, __NOW__ and __SESSION_USER__. This narrows the card; it can never widen it, because what a person may see is decided before this is read.
fields.label: Base Filters (JSON)

fields.description: Ticked, the card is clickable and opens the list holding exactly the records it counted. Unticked it is a figure and nothing more.
fields.label: Drill Enabled

name: CRM Dashboard Chart
